gaps.sentence: It took her years to ___ a living from her painting.
gaps.explanation: make a living means to earn enough money to live on.

gaps.sentence: Her company ___ a huge profit last year.
gaps.explanation: make a profit (or make a loss) is the fixed business collocation.

gaps.sentence: The children ___ great fun at the fair.
The two sides struggled to ___ an agreement before the deadline.
Halfway through the film, the children were fast ___.
gaps.explanation: fast asleep means completely asleep; it is the fixed collocation with 'fast'.

gaps.sentence: Please ___ your seats; the performance is about to begin.
gaps.explanation: take your seats is the formal way of asking people to sit down.

gaps.sentence: The regulator has ___ its warning that the scheme may be unlawful.
Shall we split it, or will you ___ the bill?
gaps.explanation: pay the bill is the fixed collocation in restaurants; 'spend the bill' is wrong.
